nodes.title: Prompt-writer instructions (advanced)
widgets_values:
You write image descriptions for a text-to-image model. The user message holds an idea inside <idea> tags.

TASK: Turn the idea into ONE paragraph of 140 to 180 words that describes a single photograph. Open with the subject and what they are doing. Then cover pose and expression, clothing, the setting from foreground to background, light, and colours. Every sentence states something visible in the frame. Keep every fact from the idea exactly as given and add only details that fit it naturally. Describe the scene itself only; the camera and film look are added elsewhere.

EXAMPLE
<idea>a man repairing a bicycle on a wet pavement</idea>
A middle-aged man in a faded green raincoat crouches beside an upturned bicycle, one hand steadying the rear wheel while the other turns a small wrench on the axle. His brow is furrowed in concentration and rain beads on his dark cap. The pavement glistens around him, reflecting the amber glow of a shopfront whose shutters are half lowered. Behind him a row of terraced houses fades into soft grey drizzle, with a red postbox standing at the corner. Cool daylight falls evenly from an overcast sky, picking out the chrome of the spokes and the wet sheen on his sleeves. Muted greens, greys and a single warm amber highlight give the street a quiet, lived-in mood.

nodes.title: Use refined image (or first pass if polish is off)
1b. PICK YOUR LOOK - switch ONE on

widgets_values:
START HERE  (Moss nostalgia workflow v5)

1.  Write your idea in 1a and tick the row you want to use.
2.  Pick a look in 1b (switch ONE on):
    A No look / B Kodachrome / C Cheap iPhone / D Aerochrome (prompt) / E Aerochrome IR pass (EXPERIMENTAL).
3.  Pick who appears in 1i: A Caucasian / B Asian / C Off (follow the idea) / D No people.
4.  Optional: pick a camera lens in 1c (right-hand column). Off adds nothing.
5.  Optional extras (far left, 1k-1m): FACE FIX, DETAIL (SeedVR2), JPEG CRUNCH.
6.  Press Run  (Ctrl + Enter).
7.  Like it? Press KEEP on the RESULT node. Nothing is saved until you do.

Everything else is automatic.

TIPS
- 1a grows with your ideas. '- Remove Selected' deletes the ON idea, 'Undo' brings it back.
- 1c: switch 'Lens picks the ratio' on and the lens chooses a realistic crop (e.g. 85mm = 4:5). Click any ratio yourself and it switches off again.
- 1e SEED: 'New seed each run' = a new image every run. 'Keep this seed' locks it.
  +1 / -1 nudge to a close variation, 'Previous seed' goes back.
- To polish a favourite: set 1e to 'Keep this seed', then switch the second pass ON in 1g. The first pass is reused, so only the polish runs.
- Switch the second pass OFF to test ideas quickly.
- 1h picks the prompt-writer LLM. If you change model FAMILY, change its 'type' too.
- Compare speed: type a note in the TIMER REPORT node (e.g. 'gemma4, 36 steps'), run, read GENERATION TIMES. Every run is also logged to ComfyUI/output/gen_times.csv.
- Edit the text inside the LOOK boxes for your own looks. LOOK A's boxes are empty on purpose.
- LOOK E makes a normal colour photo, then an extra black-and-white INFRARED pass of the same picture, and combines them like real Aerochrome. Check 'IR layer preview': foliage should be white, sky dark. Not white enough = raise the IR PASS denoise (0.55 -> 0.65). Picture drifting = lower it.
- 1i C (Off) is the one to use when your idea names the people itself, e.g. two people of different ethnicities.
- 1j is the base negative prompt; the 1i switch adds to it.
- Prefer big buttons? Click 'Moss Studio' (top right) for the simple screen.

How the extras work
widgets_values:
EXTRAS (switch ON / OFF)

1k FACE FIX - finds faces and redraws them bigger. Best for small or far-away faces. Uses your look, so faces keep the film feel.

1l DETAIL (SeedVR2) - sharpens fine detail across the whole picture.
   detail_mix 0 = keep the original grit, 1 = full SeedVR2.
   0.4 - 0.6 keeps film / phone character. Grain is added AFTER this, so it stays.

1m JPEG CRUNCH - phone-style compression. Switch ON for any look.
   It is always on for LOOK C (iPhone) - turn 'always_on_for_iphone' off to stop that.

When a switch is OFF that step does not run at all, so it costs no time.
